headline: COPPER CRACKS $14,050: 200k Tonnes Hit US Ports In July — Tariff Clock Overdue; Hormuz And China Squeeze Concentrate
snippet: Copper hit $14,050 per tonne on August 4, 2026 — its highest in two months — as US ports received more than 200,000 tonnes of copper imports in July, the largest monthly volume since 2014, as traders front-run a Trump tariff decision now overdue since June 30. The stockpiling dynamic tightened global supply routes, compounding existing concentrate shortages caused by sulphuric acid supply restrictions from the Strait of Hormuz and China's export ban on SX-EW chemical inputs suppressing copper cathode output in Chile and the DRC. For copper junior investors, the $14,050 print establishes a new 2026 high watermark that lifts NPV assumptions across every development-stage copper project — and the tariff-driven stockpiling surge illustrates what US domestic copper demand looks like when buyers position ahead of a major trade policy shift.

headline: SSR MINING Q2: $137M NET INCOME, $50M FCF At $2,622 AISC — 450-535k GEO On Track; Costs Heading To Top End
snippet: SSR Mining Inc. (Nasdaq/TSX: SSRM) reported Q2 2026 results on August 4, 2026 with production of 101,959 gold equivalent ounces at all-in sustaining costs of $2,622 per payable ounce — generating net income of $137 million ($0.66 per diluted share), operating cash flow of $115.6 million, and free cash flow of $50.3 million. The company is on track for its full-year guidance of 450,000–535,000 GEO, though AISC is trending toward the top end of guidance as the company accelerates capital investments in mine life extension across the portfolio. For retail investors benchmarking the gold mining environment, SSR Mining's Q2 print — roughly $1,478 per ounce of margin at the midpoint against a $4,100 realized gold price — illustrates how the current environment is generating cash returns that historically accelerate consolidation and acquisition of quality TSX-V development assets.

headline: GOLD STALLS AT $4,050 IN NFP WEEK — 52/48 September Hike Split; Friday Payrolls Set To Break The Standoff
snippet: Gold traded sideways around $4,050 on August 4, 2026 — below its 20-day EMA at $4,072 and beneath all key moving averages — as investors entered a make-or-break week of US economic data. Market pricing implies a 52.1% probability of a September Fed rate hike versus 47.9% hold, the tightest split in months, with the critical variable being Friday's July Non-Farm Payrolls. June's surprise miss at 57,000 jobs clashes with the Fed's hawkish 9-3 vote at its July meeting, and analysts are modeling two distinct scenarios: a sub-100,000 payroll print that kills September hike expectations and triggers a gold squeeze toward $4,150+, or a 150,000+ print that reinforces the dollar's strength and pushes gold below the $4,025 support that central bank accumulation has defended since June.

headline: PINNACLE SILVER HITS 26.1 g/t Au AND 511 g/t Ag At El Potrero — 93m Historic Vein Strike Opened In Durango (TSX-V: PINN)
snippet: Pinnacle Silver and Gold Corp. (TSX-V: PINN, OTCQB: PSGCF) announced August 4, 2026 that rehabilitation of historic underground workings at its El Potrero property in Durango, Mexico has exposed approximately 93 metres of previously inaccessible vein strike at the Dos de Mayo Norte area. Among 150 channel samples, highlights included 26.1 g/t gold and 511 g/t silver over 0.5 metres and 10.76 g/t Au and 215 g/t Ag over 1.3 metres in the South Raise — extending the Dos de Mayo vein system approximately 35 metres above the mine's main level. At silver above $58/oz and gold above $4,100, the combination of high-grade gold-silver in a vein system with demonstrated underground infrastructure represents the type of production-ready asset that historically attracts acquirer attention from mid-tier precious metals producers generating record margins.

headline: NEXUS MINERALS CRUSADER-TEMPLAR UP 70% To 304koz At Diggers — 5.67Mt @ 1.7 g/t Au In Open-Pit Shell (ASX: NXM)
snippet: Nexus Minerals Limited (ASX: NXM) presented at the Diggers & Dealers Mining Forum in Kalgoorlie on August 4, 2026 with an updated JORC 2012 Mineral Resource Estimate for the Crusader-Templar deposit at its Wallbrook Gold Project in Western Australia: 5.67 million tonnes at 1.7 g/t Au for 304,000 ounces of contained gold (0.4 g/t cut-off), representing a 70% increase in contained gold ounces from the prior resource estimate, with 46% of material in the Indicated category within an optimised open-pit shell. The Pinnacles deposit on the same tenement provides additional higher-grade underground mining exposure. For ASX gold investors, the 70% resource increase at Crusader-Templar at the sector's flagship annual conference establishes a credible open-pit development case in WA at a moment when gold above $4,100 is compressing the cost curve across the state's emerging producers.

headline: SILVER HOLDS $58+ AS IRAN ESCALATION STAYS PAUSED — $59.50 In Early NY Trade; $21 Above Year-Ago Price
snippet: Silver futures reached $59.50 per ounce in early New York trading on August 4, 2026 — up 69 cents from the prior day and more than $21 higher than a year ago — as the metal held above the key $58 support level following Saudi Arabia's pressure on President Trump to suspend planned Iran airstrikes in favour of diplomacy. The geopolitical pause removed an oil-inflation catalyst that had been suppressing precious metals sentiment, while structural silver demand from solar panel and electronics manufacturing remains intact. Coin and bar retail demand is running approximately 18% higher year-over-year, and analysts following the gold-to-silver ratio closely argue a significant ratio compression is overdue — particularly if Friday's Non-Farm Payrolls print softens September Fed hike expectations.

headline: URANIUM TERM PRICE: 18-YEAR HIGH At $94/LB While Spot Sits At $86 — $8 Gap Signals Utility Buyers Expect Higher Prices
snippet: Uranium's term price has reached an 18-year high of $94 per pound while spot uranium consolidates at $85–87, creating an $8 divergence between the two markets that reflects a structural shift in utility contracting behavior: approximately 80% of global uranium is sold through long-term contracts, and utilities are locking in future delivery at $94/lb because they expect spot prices to rise substantially, not because $94 represents fair value today. With 440 operable nuclear reactors globally requiring fuel regardless of price — since uranium is a small fraction of plant operating costs — and reactor capacity expanding from AI data centre power demand and nuclear commitments in the US, UK, and EU, the term price leading spot by $8 is the clearest forward signal available in the uranium market and the most relevant metric for junior uranium developers awaiting mine construction financing decisions.

headline: NFP WEEK: GOLD BEARS HAVE EDGE After 9-3 Fed Split — Breakdown Risk If July Payrolls Print Above 150k
snippet: Broker Elev8 published analysis ahead of August 2026 NFP week arguing that the Federal Reserve's hawkish 9-3 vote at its July meeting has shifted the structural risk for gold to the downside heading into Friday's July Non-Farm Payrolls release. The key threshold is 150,000 jobs: a print above that level raises September hike probability above 60%, strengthens the dollar, and likely pushes XAU/USD below the $4,025 support level that has held since June. The opposite scenario — a sub-100,000 print like June's 57,000 surprise — would shift September pricing to a hold and trigger the short squeeze gold bulls have been positioned for. The analysis is notable for explicitly framing NFP week as a binary event for the gold complex: regardless of Iran, regardless of central bank accumulation, the data print on Friday determines the next 3% directional move in the metal that underlies most junior mining stock valuations.

headline: HM EXPLORATION DRILLS 18.45m AT 1.14% Cu / 2.42% Zn In Phase 1 At Lewis Pilley's — Newfoundland VMS Hits 149 g/t Ag In Lower Lens (CSE: HM)
snippet: HM Exploration Corp. (CSE: HM) reported Phase 1 drilling results from the Lewis Pilley's Project in Newfoundland, Canada, with highlight intervals including 18.45 metres at 1.14% copper, 2.42% zinc, 16.74 g/t silver, and 0.32 g/t gold in the Upper Lens, and 5.42 metres at 1.99% copper, 1.66% zinc, 15.39 g/t silver, and 0.8 g/t gold in the Lower Lens. Individual sample intervals within the holes returned grades up to 8.14% copper and 27.3% zinc in the upper lens, and 149 g/t silver and 10.23 g/t gold in the lower lens — suggesting a high-grade, polymetallic VMS system with distinct vertical zonation. The Lewis Pilley's copper-zinc-silver-gold results fit the geological template of Newfoundland's prolific VMS corridor, which hosts world-class deposits at Rambler, Duck Pond, and the historic Buchans mine, and position HM Exploration for follow-up drilling targeting the high-grade core.

headline: LITHIUM FALLS TO 6-MONTH LOW: CNY 140,000 — CATL Mine Back Online Plus MinRes And Core Lithium Restart Flood Supply
snippet: Lithium carbonate traded at CNY 140,000 per tonne on August 4, 2026 — its lowest level in nearly six months — as global supply returned from multiple directions simultaneously. CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Jiangxi Province, which sat idle since August 2025 following a permit expiry, restarted production on June 29 with an annual capacity of roughly 100,000 tonnes (approximately 46,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent, or about 3% of 2025 global output); Mineral Resources restarted its Bald Hill operation in Western Australia after an 18-month suspension; and Core Lithium recommenced operations at Finniss in the Northern Territory. The combined supply return against a backdrop of softer-than-expected EV consumption growth in China is compressing prices toward the lower end of the range that makes most hard-rock lithium projects outside China economically marginal — a price signal that narrows capital availability for TSX-V and ASX lithium explorers targeting resource growth in the current market.
